query: For CrFeCoNiX high-entropy alloys (X = Si, Mn, or Al) in a single- or multiphase metallic solid-solution state, what single testable mechanistic hypothesis could explain whether a stable, coherent protective oxide layer forms and persists during exposure above 900 °C in an oxidative or corrosive atmosphere, rather than developing unstable surface oxides that crack or spall? Specify what governs the behaviour and why, a controlled comparison against a defined baseline, the predicted differences, the applicable exposure and material-state boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a falsifying observation.

generation.hypothesis: In CrFeCoNiX high-entropy alloys, adding a controlled amount of silicon encourages the formation of a coherent, silica-enriched oxide layer that remains stable during exposure above 900 °C in oxidative or corrosive atmospheres, whereas alloys with low silicon content or higher amounts of Mn or Al form mixed oxides that crack or spall.
generation.material_initial_state: CrFeCoNiX alloys in a single-phase metallic solid-solution state
generation.intervention: Systematically vary the alloying element content to compare alloys with high silicon content versus those with minimal silicon (with otherwise similar compositions)
generation.conditions: Exposure at temperatures above 900 °C in an oxidative and corrosive environment
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of a coherent, silica-enriched oxide layer
generation.mechanism: Silicon promotes the preferential formation of a protective silica-based oxide that exhibits lower internal stresses and improved adhesion compared to the heterogeneous oxide scales formed when Mn or Al are predominant along with the base metals
generation.predicted_outcome: Alloys with increased silicon content will develop a stable, coherent protective oxide layer that persists under high-temperature oxidative conditions, while low-silicon alloys will form unstable, cracked, or spalled oxide scales
generation.baseline: CrFeCoNiX alloys with minimal silicon content
generation.boundary: The hypothesis applies to single-phase metallic solid solutions of CrFeCoNiX and is valid for long-term exposure (>100 hours) at temperatures above 900 °C in oxidative atmospheres
generation.uncertainty: While the mechanistic role of silicon in promoting protective oxide formation is supported by prior studies, the interplay with other elements (especially Mn and Al) in multiphase systems or under variable exposure durations remains uncertain

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of CrFeCoNiX alloys differing only in silicon content (high-silicon vs low-silicon) while keeping other elements constant. Expose both sets to a controlled oxidative and corrosive atmosphere at 950 °C for 100 hours.
measurements: Characterize the oxide scale morphology and continuity using scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and transmission electron microscopy (TEM)
Determine the chemical composition and phase distribution of the oxide layers using X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) and energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDX)
Assess the adherence and mechanical integrity of the oxide scales through thermal cycling and scratch adhesion tests
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If high-silicon alloys do not exhibit significantly improved oxide scale coherence, adhesion, and resistance to cracking or spallation compared to low-silicon alloys under identical exposure conditions, then the hypothesis is falsified

chosen.approach: Alloying element addition to promote protective oxide scale formation
